market_story: import: MISO's PJM seam is a purchased-power tie whose bands clear against the hour's actual PJM western-border price, so the seam imports MOST when MISO's own price is LOW relative to PJM — the measured seam's behaviour (corr(flow, MISO DA) -0.04 to -0.14, positive decile slope). A ladder frozen to an annual quantile leaves merit exactly when MISO's price falls, which is backwards; the hourly anchor lets the shallow bands (negative delta_k) clear through MISO's cheap hours and the deep bands price out in its expensive ones. CT_PEAKER / COAL: imports leaving the expensive hours are served by MISO's own peakers and coal in those hours (CT_PEAKER +1.1 TWh in 2023/2024, COAL_PRB +1.1-1.4 TWh), which is where the C1 record shows them short; no floor or offer moved. CC_REGULAR-2023 (-5.92 -> -6.31) and CC_CHP-2024 (-0.51 -> -0.73) give back a little of that energy — reported, not explained away. The mechanism adds no import energy (annual gross imports fall 1.5-3.5 TWh per year); it moves it to the hours the measured seam flows.
